The main takeaway from our work is that

the construction of new state spaces is a complex, contingent and contested process, which involves a range of political actors, institutions and processes, and which is shaped by the pre-existing scalar and spatial selectivities of the state and its institutionalised practices of state spatial and scalar restructuring.

the reconfiguration of regional uneven development in Belgium is not simply a matter of the “new regionalism” or “regionalism” as such, but rather the product of the complex interplay between the hegemonic projects and state spatial selectivities of the Belgian national state and the Flemish regional state.
regional uneven development is a key driver for reconfigurations of state space, which is a highly political process.
